summary: Scoped starting-point critique on RAG draft
hypothesis: Scoping the second-pass critique to a single, well-defined failure mode — whether the draft establishes the user's starting point — should avoid the over-broad audit failures of exp005/exp017 and recover lost coverage without corrupting the other six slots.
technique: A two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 reuses the exp011 contrastive RAG draft (best baseline). Stage 2 is a single FM call scoped exclusively to detecting whether any of the 7 slots establishes the user's starting point; if yes the draft is returned verbatim, if no the call names the single weakest slot and writes one replacement question, then Swift swaps exactly that one slot deterministically (all others unchanged).
result: Scored 0.273 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), a regression of −0.050 vs the exp011 best (0.323) and −0.034 vs the baseline (0.307); rubric atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3. The scoped critique mostly mis-fired — the 3B judged startingPointCovered=TRUE when it was FALSE, so the protective gate rarely triggered, and in the cases where it did swap the replacement question was generic/off-target rather than the sharp gold question. Hypothesis falsified: the failure is not audit breadth but the 3B's inability to detect or fill the missing dimension, confirming the multi-FM wall holds; discarded.
